title: Dimensional Assessment of Personality Pathology and Treatment Adaptation in Alcohol Use Disorder: From an Empty Systematic Review to a Narrative Synthesis
content: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) and personality disorders (PD) co-occur in up to two thirds of treatment-seeking patients, and comorbidity predicts poorer engagement and relapse. Current diagnostic frameworks (DSM-5 Alternative Model, ICD-11, HiTOP) describe personality pathology dimensionally, which is expected to be less stigmatizing, more acceptable to patients and more useful for treatment planning. We aimed to identify programs that assess personality dimensionally in patients with AUD and adapt treatment to the profile obtained. Following a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD420260656442), PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (February–March 2025). Of 2,529 records, 72 were assessed in full text; none met the pre-specified criteria, so the review was converted into a narrative synthesis of the 44 closest reports plus one case report identified outside the search. Reports fell into three groups: dimensional assessment without consequences for treatment; treatment adapted to a categorical PD diagnosis (schema, psychodynamic or mentalization-based therapies) or transdiagnostic treatments that did not assess personality; and contextual evidence on comorbidity, typologies and assessment. The only near-miss relied on a categorical Millon inventory. We discuss why assessment and intervention remain disconnected and propose brief dimensional screening at treatment entry as a pathway to person-centered, less stigmatizing AUD care.
